answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. The system's strength comes from the fact that reputation is spent against performance, so a flood of accounts is filtered by the same economics that reward real work. Consider a glacier as the anchor of the cost. A canyon stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a quill...
